sentences.text: Iteravis is an extinct ornithuromorph bird discovered in the Early Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation of Liaoning Province, China.
The species name honors Dr. Fritz Huchzermeyer, an archosaur paleontologist who passed away just before the genus was officially described.
Fossil evidence suggests this creature consumed larger food particles than the earlier Archaeorhynchus, though its exact diet remains unclear.
In 2018, researchers identified three new specimens from the Sihedang locality that, combined with older fossils, represent the only known ornithurines from that specific site.
This animal lived during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous, a period spanning between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
Scientists currently debate whether Iteravis is merely a synonym of Gansus zheni or a distinct genus closely related to Gansus within the family Gansuidae.
In 2021, Ju and colleagues concluded that Iteravis huchzermeyeri and Gansus zheni are the same species based on a detailed comparison.
Conversely, O'Connor and colleagues (2021) treated Iteravis huchzermeyeri and Gansus zheni as distinct species despite observing small differences of uncertain taxonomic significance.
Recent phylogenetic analyses by Wang et al. (2025) and Huang et al. (2026) recovered Iteravis as the sister taxon to Gansus yumenensis.
